definitions.explanation: A collection of various items packed together in one box or package, typically food items such as sweets, cookies, or fruits. Very common as gifts in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: ⟦クッキー→クッキー：10798_kukkii⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{買|か}った→買う：00489_kau⟧。
examples.english: I bought an assortment of cookies.

examples.japanese: ⟦お{歳暮|せいぼ}→お歳暮：06126_oseibo⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦フルーツ→フルーツ：11247_furuutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{贈|おく}った→贈る：09862_okuru⟧。
examples.english: I sent a fruit assortment as a year-end gift.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧⟦{和菓子|わがし}→和菓子：04962_wagashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{手土産|てみやげ}→手土産：08353_temiyage⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦ぴったり→ぴったり：02362_pittari⟧だ。
examples.english: This assortment of Japanese sweets is perfect as a gift to bring when visiting.

notes:
USAGE:
{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ is extremely common in the context of gift-giving and shopping. Japanese gift culture relies heavily on boxed assortments of food items. The word comes from ⟦{詰|つ}める→詰める：02078_tsumeru⟧ (to pack) and ⟦{合|あ}わせる→合わせる：01872_awaseru⟧ (to combine), literally meaning items packed together. It almost always refers to food items.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- ⟦お{菓子|かし}→お菓子：02852_okashi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ: assortment of sweets
- ⟦フルーツ→フルーツ：11247_furuutsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ: fruit assortment
- {詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ⟦セット→セット：03853_setto⟧: assortment set
- {詰|つ}め{合|あ}わせ⟦ギフト→ギフト：10824_gifuto⟧: assortment gift box
